title: When your care ends
respondents: People whose care with us has ended for a reason other than death; their representative where the person has moved or cannot be reached
summary: Asked about 2 weeks after care ends: why it ended, anything the person was unhappy about, how we handled the ending, passing information to a new provider, returning keys, and whether they would come back. Named, about 9 minutes.
purpose: Learns why people stop using our service, whether the ending was handled safely and well, and what they would tell us now that they no longer depend on us. It is a later, more considered view than the conversation the Care Coordinator holds when a person ends their care, never a replacement for it. It asks the main reason care ended, what the person was unhappy about (using the same themes as our other feedback, so results join the theme reporting), how well we handled the end, whether we passed the information a new provider needed, whether we returned keys, and whether they would want our care again. Results feed the quarterly governance report as endings by reason, the monthly feedback summary and improvement actions, and evidence Regulation 17(2)(e) (seeking and acting on feedback) and the CQC quality statements on continuity of care and on learning.

timing.when: About 10 working days after the last visit; never after a death
timing.trigger: The person's care with us ending

introduction:
Your care with {{organisation}} has ended. We would like to know why, how we handled the ending, and what we could do better for the people we still support. It takes about 9 minutes.

Taking part is up to you. Your answers are linked to your name only so we can put things right, for example if something was missed when your care ended. Your former care workers (carers) will not see them.

This survey is not for urgent concerns. If you are worried about your safety or someone else's, or need help now, phone the office, or contact your council's adult social care team. In an emergency, call 999.
privacyNotice:
{{organisation}} uses your answers to put right anything missed when your care ended and to improve our service. Our legal reason for using your answers is our legitimate interest in running a good, safe service.

Your answers are linked to your name. They are seen only by our Registered Manager, Deputy Manager, safeguarding lead, Care Coordinators and the office staff who follow them up, never by your care workers (carers), and reports show combined results only. If you tell us someone may be at risk of harm, we may tell the council to keep them safe.

We keep your answers for 3 years after this survey, under our Records Management and Retention Policy. You can ask to see, correct or delete your answers, or object to our using them. To do this, or to complain about how we use your information, contact the office or our Data Protection Officer (details on our website). You can also complain to the Information Commission.

howToRun: Ask this survey about 10 working days after the last visit, once only, with one reminder after a week. It never replaces the conversation the Care Coordinator holds within 1 working day when a person ends their care, under the Visit Cancellations and Refusals of Care Procedure.

CareFlow cannot start a survey when a package ends, so the Care Coordinator puts a reminder in the office diary on the day of the last visit. Send it with Send or schedule, Chosen people, in a running copy of this template: people whose care ended in the last 3 months (they show as Care ended) can still be chosen by name, with no reason needed for this survey. CareFlow emails them their own link at the personal email on their record, never through the portal, and texts them if Text message is ticked in Reminders and follow-up. Every invitation and reminder to someone whose care has ended carries "unsubscribe from all surveys": it stops every survey message to them for good, staff cannot undo it, and replying STOP to a text does the same. Otherwise office staff who were not in the person's core care team, and not the Care Coordinator who held the ending conversation, phone the person and enter the answers with Record response, channel Telephone, or post a printed copy in the person's recorded format with a prepaid envelope and enter it with Record response on the day it comes back. By default only managers and admins can record survey answers ("Record survey responses") and only managers can send or open a survey: give these to the staff who make these calls; Care Coordinators can only view surveys unless given them.

Never send it after a death (use the family survey after a death, SUR-FAM-002); where the service ended under the Violence and Aggression Towards Staff Policy; while a safeguarding enquiry involving the person is open; when care is only paused for a hospital stay; when the person moved to another of our branches; or when they said they want no further contact. If a complaint is open, ask the after-complaint questions (SUR-PWS-006) when it closes instead.

Where the person moved to a care home or cannot be reached, invite the representative recorded in their care plan, with the person's permission where they have capacity, and record who answered in CareFlow's "Who is answering" field. Read each question, its help text and every answer choice exactly as written; the reason lists are long, which is why it takes about 9 minutes. An easy read version has a picture for each reason.
Cancel any quality check, check-in or other survey that was due after the ending; check the person's survey history in CareFlow.

Who may open individual answers: office staff who make or follow up the calls, and the Registered Manager and Deputy Manager. This is set in Who can see the answers: individual responses are limited to the Registered Manager, the Deputy Manager, Care Coordinators and the safeguarding lead, and results to the same staff, showing from 5 answers. Super Admin, Admin and the person who made the survey can always see both, so keep those roles to staff who may open them. Add the role of the office staff who make or follow up the calls.
actingOnResults: Office staff pass every answer that needs action to the Care Coordinator or Registered Manager the same working day, and the alerts below apply.

How to count: report endings by main reason, each quarter, beside the packages ended after a hospital stay; the unhappy-about answers use the same themes as the monthly feedback summary (timekeeping and visit length; continuity; communication and the office; staff attitude, dignity and respect; personal care; medicines; fairness, culture and identity; safety; other), with cost added. For the other questions report the share answering Very good or Good, or Yes, leaving out Does not apply to me, "We did not hold any keys" and Don't know, and show how many people answered.
Review the reason list after a year of "Other" answers. Never report a group of fewer than 5 people separately.

Keep individual answers for 3 years after the survey under the Records Management and Retention Policy. For CQC, the endings by reason and the actions taken evidence learning from people who leave and safe endings and handovers (Regulation 17(2)(e)).

alerts.when: Any comment suggesting the person is now without the care they need, or at risk.
alerts.action: The Registered Manager decides the same working day whether to raise a safeguarding or self-neglect concern, under the Visit Cancellations and Refusals of Care Procedure, the Safeguarding Concerns: Reporting, Referral and Enquiry Procedure and the Self-Neglect and Hoarding Procedure. For a commissioned package, tell the commissioner the same working day so it can review the person's needs.

alerts.when: "Did we give back any keys we held for your home?" answered No.
alerts.action: The Care Coordinator arranges the return of keys against a signature and confirms the key safe code is removed from CareFlow the same working day, under the Key Holding, Key Safes and Access to People's Homes Procedure; both were due within 5 working days of the last visit, so record the late return in the incident log under the Incident Reporting, Investigation and Learning Policy.

rule.task: Keys not returned: arrange return and remove key safe code

alerts.when: "Did we give your new care provider the information they needed?" answered No.
alerts.action: The Care Coordinator sends the new provider the information it needs within 1 working day (it was due before the new provider's first visit), as the Confidentiality and Information Sharing Policy allows, and records the late handover in the incident log under the Incident Reporting, Investigation and Learning Policy.

rule.task: New provider not given information: send it now

alerts.when: "What was the main reason your care with us ended?" answered "I was not happy with the care", or any answer to "Was there anything you were unhappy about?" other than Nothing, with no clear request.
alerts.action: A Care Coordinator, where possible not the one who held the ending conversation, contacts the person within 5 working days and offers to take it as a complaint. People who have left can still complain.

rule.task: Unhappy when care ended: offer to take a complaint

alerts.when: "What was the main reason your care with us ended?" answered "You told me you could no longer provide my care", with a comment linking it to a complaint.
alerts.action: The Registered Manager checks that the hand-back record says why the decision is unconnected to the complaint and tells the Nominated Individual, whose approval is needed to end the service of someone who complained in the previous 6 months, under the Complaints Policy and Procedure.

alerts.when: A comment expressing dissatisfaction that needs a response, or overall experience or the handling of the ending answered Poor or Very poor.
alerts.action: Dissatisfaction that needs a response is a complaint: record it the same working day, grade it within 1 working day and acknowledge it within 3 working days under the Complaints Policy and Procedure. If unsure, treat it as a complaint.

rule.task: Poor experience or ending: record dissatisfaction

alerts.when: Any comment suggesting abuse or neglect while in our care, or "Not feeling safe" chosen.
alerts.action: Pass it to the safeguarding lead the same working day; the lead assesses the risk within 1 hour and refers to the local authority where needed, under the Safeguarding Concerns: Reporting, Referral and Enquiry Procedure. A concern about a member of staff also follows the Managing Allegations Against Staff Procedure.

rule.task: Did not feel safe in our care: possible safeguarding concern

alerts.when: "Would you like someone to contact you about your answers?" answered Yes.
alerts.action: Office staff who were not in the person's core care team contact them within 5 working days in the way they prefer and record what was agreed.

rule.task: Asked to be contacted about their answers

alerts.when: An answer to "What did we do well?", or any comment praising our service or a named member of staff.
alerts.action: Record it as a compliment in CareFlow the same working day; the Field Care Supervisor or line manager passes it to each employee named within 5 working days, under the Compliments, Feedback and Involvement Procedure.

Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014, Regulation 12(2)(i): working with others so that care is safe when people move between services
NICE NG21 Home care, recommendation 1.4.7: recognise that major changes, such as moving from home care to personal assistants, can make people feel unsafe
NHS England, Using the Friends and Family Test to improve patient experience (version 2): feedback a few weeks after leaving a service is more considered than feedback straight away
